title: Keyboard Manager: Attempting to remap the Dual Screen Project key chooses character P

status.label: Need keyboard and current key-capture details
status.detail: The 0.91.1 report does not identify the keyboard model or whether the physical Project key emits P outside Keyboard Manager.

next_action: Request a current-build retest and keyboard-specific key-capture control before changing virtual-key selection behavior.

judgment.rationale: The report says selecting the Dual Screen “Project” key in Keyboard Manager selects P, but gives no keyboard model or capture control. Without knowing whether the physical key itself emits P outside the editor, the failure could be a keyboard/driver mapping or a Keyboard Manager UI lookup. Request a current-build retest and exact hardware/key identity before proposing a code change.
evidence: The issue lists PowerToys 0.91.1 and Windows 11 Pro 24H2.
The report says selecting the Dual Screen “Project” key selects P and would also map P.
The issue has no comments and does not identify the keyboard model, key location, or behavior outside Keyboard Manager.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the keyboard model and a current-build comparison showing whether the physical Project key emits P outside Keyboard Manager; collect a fresh bug report only if the editor still misidentifies it.

fix_assessment.rationale: The physical key and its input code are unidentified, and the issue has no current-build control test. A code fix cannot be distinguished from a keyboard/driver mapping until those facts are supplied.

issue_context.summary: Selecting a keyboard’s Dual Screen “Project” key in Keyboard Manager reportedly captures it as P.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.91.1 and Windows 11 Pro 24H2.
The reporter says the Project key is selected as P and that P is then included in the remapping.
There are no comments, and the keyboard model and behavior outside Keyboard Manager are not specified.
inferences: The key may be translated to P by the device/driver or by Keyboard Manager’s key-selection path; the current evidence does not distinguish them.
issue_context.analysis: The key identity and a no-remap input control are the discriminating evidence. Ask for the exact keyboard and current behavior before investigating a scan-code or key-picker change.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report; it has no comments, assignee, or linked fix.
No evidence in the report identifies the physical keyboard, the Project key location, or what code the key emits outside Keyboard Manager.

information_gaps.information: The exact keyboard model/key identity and whether pressing the Project key types P in another app without a remap on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes a keyboard/driver translation from a Keyboard Manager key-picker defect.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Retest with no mapping configured, identify the keyboard model and key label/location, and compare the captured behavior in another app.

information_gaps.information: A fresh diagnostic archive captured immediately after the current-build picker selects P for the Project key.
information_gaps.why_needed: If the key is still misidentified inside Keyboard Manager after the hardware control is checked, the current module configuration can help triage it.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: If it persists on the current build, comment /bugreport immediately after reproducing.

comment.body:
Thanks for reporting that the Dual Screen “Project” key is selected as P. The issue is from 0.91.1 and does not identify the keyboard model or whether the physical key emits P outside Keyboard Manager. Could you please:
1. Retest on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer and provide the keyboard model and exact label/location of the Project key.
2. Give numbered steps for selecting it in Keyboard Manager and say whether pressing it types P in another app when no remap is configured.
3. If the current build still captures it as P, comment `/bugreport` immediately after reproducing.
This will distinguish a keyboard/driver scan-code mapping from a Keyboard Manager selection issue.
